headline: The AI for Math Fund has grown to $35.1 million, with new grants for open tools that check AI-made proofs.
score_reason: Funding news for open AI tools in mathematics; a real announcement, with no outside review of the results yet.
importance_line: It means more money for open tools that let mathematicians inspect and verify AI-made proofs, but the grants run for 12 to 24 months and their results are not yet known.
summary: EdTech Innovation Hub reports that Renaissance Philanthropy and XTX Markets, a financial firm, added $17.1 million to the AI for Math Fund, bringing its total to $35.1 million. The fund chose 22 projects from more than 470 applications, covering AI help with theorem proving (checking that mathematical arguments are valid), datasets and tools for testing AI in mathematics.
notes: Full text read. Named people with position: Tom Kalil (CEO of Renaissance Philanthropy); Simon Coyle (Head of Philanthropy at XTX Markets). Kumar Garg (President at Renaissance Philanthropy) and Alex Gerko (founder of XTX Markets) appear in the text and are mentioned only as the outlet describes them.
